items.reason: 140/6 = 23.3 is correct, but it isn't the all-time high: 1967 UCLA averaged 23.75 (Wyoming 109–60, Pacific 80–64, Houston 73–58, Dayton 79–64). It's the best of the 64/68-team era, ahead of 1996 Kentucky at 21.5.

items.new: Most consecutive NCAA tournament wins by double digits: 12 (2023–2024)
items.reason: From Sports-Reference: UConn won 24 straight non-conference games (including NCAA) by 10+ points, but the streak ran Nov 7, 2022 (Stonehill) to Nov 27, 2023 (New Hampshire) and ended with the Dec 1, 2023 loss at Kansas, so '2022–2024' is wrong. I also found no source calling that streak an NCAA record. The documented NCAA record is 12 straight NCAA tournament wins by double figures (all 12 games of 2023 and 2024), per UConn's official notes ('a March Madness record'). If you'd rather keep the 24-game stat, change the years to Nov. 2022–Nov. 2023 and move it out of the NCAA-records list.
